title: SYSK Selects: How Ghosts Work
summary: Halloween rerun of the classic Stuff You Should Know episode "How Ghosts Work," released as part of SYSK Selects. Josh opens with a personal-ghost-story setup and Chuck describes a 'ghost' sighting he and friend Brett had at an intersection in Athens, Georgia: a motionless elderly woman in a black robe and purple sash holding a Bible, who vanished. The hosts then survey ghost belief (a 2009 CBS News poll says about 40 percent of Americans believe), famous ghost photographs (Freddie Jackson, the Lady of Brown Hall fire-girl photo, the Old West Boot Hill photo, the Google Earth 'murder' that turned out to be a dog), orbs in photos, ghosts tied to places (Hotel del Coronado), mediums and fraud, Victorian psychical research and William James, ectoplasm, energy and quantum-particle theories of what ghosts are, Richard Wiseman's research on haunted locations, hallucination explanations (grief, sleep paralysis, hypnagogic states), temperature drops and humidity, electromagnetic fields and the temporal lobe, the magnetosphere, and infrasound (Vladimir Gavreau and the Ghost in the Machine case). They close with a critique of the claim that paranormal belief reduces critical thinking. The episode ends with listener mail from teacher Sierra Benton about a road trip car game and the sign-off."

segments.title: Halloween intro and horror contest banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Halloween SYSK Selects rerun of How Ghosts Work, recorded in July, and he and Chuck banter about the horror fiction contest.

segments.title: Chuck's ghost sighting in Athens, Georgia
segments.summary: Chuck describes driving with friend Brett through Five Points in Athens, Georgia, and seeing a motionless elderly woman in a black robe and purple sash holding a Bible in an intersection. She vanished when they looked back, and both friends described the same figure.

segments.title: Ghost belief and famous ghost photos
segments.summary: The hosts note about 40 percent of Americans believe in ghosts per a 2009 CBS News poll, and discuss how ghosts are impossible to disprove. They turn to famous ghost photographs, including Freddie Jackson, the Old West cemetery photo, and the fire-girl image explained as smoke and light, and the Google Earth 'murder' that was a dog.

segments.title: Why ghosts appear and ghosts tied to places
segments.summary: The hosts discuss reasons ghosts supposedly appear, such as delivering news or being earthbound, and cite the two ghost women at the Hotel del Coronado and haunted hotels.

segments.title: Mediums, psychical research, and debunking
segments.summary: They discuss mediums who may be frauds or sincere, and the history of psychical research societies, including William James and debunking of Victorian-era mediums, and how modern science has largely stopped investigating ghosts.

segments.title: Orbs in photographs
segments.summary: Josh describes an orb photo he took of his dogs, which his wife believes is their late grandfather, and explains skeptical explanations such as camera flash reflection, lens spots, and sensor defects.

segments.title: What ghosts are made of: energy and quantum theories
segments.summary: The hosts discuss theories that ghosts are energy that is transferred, ectoplasm in Victorian times, and quantum particles that can tunnel through solid matter, and ask why some people become ghosts and others do not.

segments.title: Richard Wiseman's haunted-location research
segments.summary: Richard Wiseman at the University of Hertfordshire mapped sighting locations and physical conditions, finding that people unaware of a site's haunted history still reported sightings in the same specific areas. The hosts also mention parapsychology programs at Duke, UCLA, and the University of Edinburgh.

segments.title: Hallucinations, cold spots, EMF, and infrasound
segments.summary: The hosts cover hallucination explanations such as grief, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic trance, plus cold spots and humidity, electromagnetic fields affecting the brain, the magnetosphere, and infrasound as a source of dread and visual effects, including the Ghost in the Machine case and Gavreau's lab.

segments.title: Critical thinking and paranormal belief
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a claim by the National Science Board that paranormal belief reduces critical thinking, and Brian Dunning's skeptical approach. They close the main topic and point listeners to the Tracy Wilson article on How Stuff Works.

segments.title: Listener mail from Sierra Benton
segments.summary: A middle school teacher describes driving students to Space Academy and playing a car game called Pass Around the Ether Rag with potty words that produced silly names like the poop fusion.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to tweet, join Facebook, or email, and the episode ends.
